rationale: In the source, "nearby" means the people near you who will scan the code (see the instructions string). In Arabic, the adjective القريب modifies الرابط, so the heading reads "the nearby link", which means something else.
summary: The heading says "share the nearby link" instead of "share the link with people nearby".

rationale: The source and the developer comment say only that the app may close after the icon changes. "يتوقف عن العمل" usually means the app stops working or crashes. The related string restart_and_shortcuts_removal_warning_dialog_body already uses "قد يُغلَق".
summary: "May close" is rendered as "may stop working", which suggests a malfunction.

rationale: The source says "improve %1$s". Putting "خدماتنا" before the app name makes it read "improve our services Firefox", which is broken Arabic.
summary: The app name sits straight after "خدماتنا" (our services), so the sentence is ungrammatical.

rationale: The source "Enter a password" is an instruction. The matching messages for the username and web address fields are rendered "أدخل اسم مستخدم" and "أدخل عنوان ويب", so this one is inconsistent on the same screen.
summary: This error message uses a noun ("entering a password") where the matching field errors tell the user to do something.

rationale: The developer comment states %s is the name of the suggested search engine; "ابحث عن" means "search for", so the string tells the user to look up the engine rather than search with it.

rationale: The developer comment says "Search" is a verb: the screen searches within Settings. The Arabic reads as the settings for search, which names a different screen.
summary: "Search settings" (search is a verb) is rendered as the noun phrase "search settings" (settings of search).

rationale: The source means configuring an app that is already installed, not installing it. The matching 3- and 6-step strings correctly use لإعداد.

rationale: Typo; the correct word is المغلقة.

rationale: The snackbar confirms a completed action; the verbal noun reads like a "Close tab" command.

rationale: The source says 'Create a new tab'. نافذة means 'window', a different UI concept.

rationale: The comment says this button opens the Tab Search feature for searching through tabs. The current Arabic names a tab called 'search'.
summary: The Arabic reads as "open the search tab" instead of "open search in tabs".

rationale: The button opens Settings so the user can see the auto-close options. "خيارات العرض" means view/display settings, which is a different thing.

rationale: The sibling counter strings (normal, private and synced tabs) say "التبويبات" and "انقر للانتقال بين التبويبات". Screen reader users get inconsistent terms on the same surface.

rationale: Other strings address the user in the singular (يمكنك، تعرضها), so this plural form breaks the locale's established form of address.
summary: Addresses the user in the plural ("تأخذوا"), while the locale otherwise uses the singular.

rationale: "عنوان" is the indefinite direct object of the imperative أدخل, so the adjective that agrees with it has to be accusative (منصوب). In written text that ending appears as the alif tanween: صالحًا.
summary: The adjective describing the object of أدخل lacks the accusative ending; it should be صالحًا, not صالح.

rationale: In Arabic, افتقر/يفتقر takes its object through إلى. Without it the sentence is ungrammatical.
summary: The verb يفتقر is missing its required preposition إلى.

rationale: The same source term, crash report, appears as تقارير الأعطال in this dialog's body and checkbox. Using a different term on the button is inconsistent.
summary: The button calls a crash report بلاغ انهيار, while the same dialog uses تقارير الأعطال.

rationale: This string is about a single report (تقرير, masculine singular), so the pronoun must be masculine. The feminine form belongs to the plural version of this string.
summary: The pronoun in إرسالها is feminine, but it refers to the masculine singular تقرير.

rationale: "Start fresh" is an idiom for starting over. "بانتعاشة" (with a refreshment/freshness) does not convey that meaning.
summary: "start fresh" is translated literally as "start with a refreshment".

rationale: Elsewhere in this batch, browsing history is "تأريخ التصفح". "التاريخ" is ambiguous and commonly read as "date".
summary: "history" is rendered as "التاريخ" (usually "date"), unlike "تأريخ" in the other strings.

rationale: The source uses em dashes, and the locale's convention is the em dash.
summary: Hyphens are used where the source and the locale convention use em dashes.

rationale: The source tells the user to press the back button to exit fullscreen. "زر الحذف" means "delete button", so the instruction is wrong.
summary: "press back" is translated as pressing the delete button.

rationale: In Arabic orthography the conjunction و attaches to the following word.
summary: The conjunction و is written as a separate word.

rationale: "Private browsing" needs the definite noun to match the definite adjective; "تصفح الخاص" is ungrammatical.
summary: The phrase breaks noun–adjective agreement: "تصفح" has no article but the adjective "الخاص" does.

rationale: The source is an imperative ("Make %1$s your default"); the imperative of جعل takes hamzat wasl (اجعل), while أجعل is first-person present.

rationale: The source means the user's own custom list of preferred URLs. "في المفضّلة" names the Favorites/bookmarks feature, which is a different data source.

rationale: In Arabic orthography the conjunction و must be joined to the next word; a space after it is a spelling error.
summary: The conjunction و is written as a separate word instead of attached to the following word.

rationale: Mozilla is a brand that stays untranslated; other strings in the same file keep it in Latin script.
